summary_hint: New-hire offer from <employer> for <position title>, base <salary/rate> <frequency>, start date <start_date> — the future employment IN-9 verifies and the role IN-7 assesses for same-line-of-work.

typed_core.name: candidate_or_borrower_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose income this is; attaches the document to the borrower

typed_core.name: position_title
typed_core.why: IN-7 (rule reads it) — the new role, compared against employment history to judge same line of work

typed_core.name: start_date
typed_core.why: IN-9 (rule reads it) — the future/just-started employment start date the rule detects

typed_core.name: employer_legal_name
typed_core.why: identity — the employer; IN-7 same-line-of-work employer context; processor VOE

typed_core.name: employer_address
typed_core.why: processor — independent verification / VOE follow-up; employer identity

typed_core.name: employer_contact
typed_core.why: processor — independent-verification contact (name/phone/email of HR signer)

typed_core.name: base_salary_or_hourly_rate
typed_core.why: processor — income usability; IN-7 example keys on equal pay; needs pay_frequency to interpret
typed_core.prompt_hint: Distinguish base guaranteed compensation from sign-on bonus, relocation, and overtime/bonus/commission terms (those are one-time or variable and are not the qualifying base)

typed_core.name: pay_frequency
typed_core.why: disambiguator for base_salary_or_hourly_rate — annual vs hourly vs monthly changes the number's meaning
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture pay_frequency verbatim next to the rate; if hourly, capture guaranteed_hours_per_week

typed_core.name: employment_type
typed_core.why: processor — full-time/part-time/contract drives income stability and usability for IN-7/IN-9

typed_core.name: guaranteed_hours_per_week
typed_core.why: disambiguator — an hourly rate cannot be annualized without guaranteed hours

typed_core.name: document_issue_date
typed_core.why: identity/processor — when the offer was issued; IN-9 recency of the offer letter on file

typed_core.name: offer_expiration_date
typed_core.why: processor — whether the offer is still open; a lapsed offer weakens IN-9 usability

typed_core.name: start_date_confirmed_or_employment_commenced
typed_core.why: disambiguator for IN-9 — whether employment already started, which decides if a first pay stub is still required

typed_core.name: employer_signer_name_title
typed_core.why: processor — who executed the offer; authenticity / third-party independence

typed_core.name: employer_signature_and_date
typed_core.why: processor — the offer is executed by the employer; presence supports IN-9 usability

typed_core.name: candidate_acceptance_signature_and_date
typed_core.why: processor — whether the candidate accepted; an unaccepted offer is weaker evidence for IN-9
typed_core.prompt_hint: The candidate acceptance signature and the employer signature are distinct blocks; capture both dates

nested_lists.name: employment_contingencies
nested_lists.shape_reason: a handful of short strings (background check, drug screen, I-9, references); far under the 16,384-token ceiling, so a flat list is cheapest and per-field wrapping is unwarranted

fields.name: contingency
fields.why: IN-9 context — an unsatisfied contingency means the offer/income is not yet firm; extract each as listed

rejected.name: document_title
rejected.reason: classification happens before extraction; no rule/processor use

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: an offer letter is not a standardized form

rejected.name: issuer_name
rejected.reason: duplicates employer_legal_name (the offer's issuer is the employer)

rejected.name: statement_period_start, statement_period_end
rejected.reason: not applicable to an offer letter

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: covered by flattened candidate_or_borrower_name + employer fields

rejected.name: property_address, loan_number, account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: not present on an offer letter; no consumer

rejected.name: notary_block
rejected.reason: an offer letter is not notarized

rejected.name: document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: draft/final rarely stated; marginal, catch-all suffices

rejected.name: work_location
rejected.reason: no rule; marginal processor value; catch-all suffices

rejected.name: sign_on_bonus, relocation_or_allowances
rejected.reason: one-time; not qualifying base income; no rule; catch-all

rejected.name: overtime_bonus_commission_terms
rejected.reason: variable-comp terms are a judgment for IN-7, not a fact this schema should conclude; base fields + pay_frequency suffice

rejected.name: exempt_or_nonexempt_status
rejected.reason: disambiguates OT eligibility only; no consumer; catch-all

encoding_variations: pay_frequency / base_salary — the same compensation is stated as $120,000/yr, $57.69/hour, or $10,000/month; the rate is meaningless without its frequency and (for hourly) guaranteed hours. Carry pay_frequency and guaranteed_hours_per_week alongside the number.

start_date vs effective_date — offer letters may say 'start date', 'first day', or 'effective date of employment'; treat the employment commencement date as start_date (effective_date is rejected as a duplicate).
employment_type / exempt status — enums with no coercer; issuers write 'Full-Time / Exempt', 'Regular FT', 'W-2 salaried'. Degraded to str; downstream interprets.
start_date_confirmed_or_employment_commenced — a boolean with no coercer; appears as 'employment commenced', a checkbox, or an addendum. Degraded to str.

open_questions.q: employment_contingencies shape — nested flat-row string list vs flattened single str.
options: keep as a one-off nested list
open_questions.recommendation: keep flat-row for now; revisit to flatten if real offers typically list <=2 contingencies (cheaper, no bespoke plumbing)

open_questions.q: Variable pay for IN-7 — should the schema extract structured overtime/bonus/commission terms, or is that a downstream judgment?
options: leave to catch-all; IN-7 judges from base fields + pay_frequency
open_questions.recommendation: leave overtime_bonus_commission_terms to the catch-all and let IN-7 judge from base fields + pay_frequency; flag whether IN-7 needs a variable_pay_present tag rather than a structured field

open_questions.q: IN-7 field granularity — confirm position_title (raw) is the field IN-7 reads, versus a normalized job-family.
open_questions.recommendation: extract raw position_title; job-family normalization is a downstream tag, not an extraction field

open_questions.q: IN-9 first-pay-stub linkage — confirm that start_date_confirmed_or_employment_commenced as boolean-degraded-to-str is acceptable or whether a coercer/enum is warranted.
open_questions.recommendation: start_date_confirmed_or_employment_commenced is the disambiguator for whether a first pay stub is still outstanding; boolean-degraded-to-str acceptable now

notes: 16 typed-core rows — below the 20-25 target, which is expected for a Tier-2 document whose two rules key on just two fields (position_title, start_date); the remainder are identity, disambiguators, and processor-review fields. No field is padded in.
This is not a standardized form — do not expect a form number or revision date; the issuer is the employer, not an independent third party.
Contingencies (background/drug/I-9/references) indicate the offer is not yet firm — extract each as listed.

No new _PII_FIELDS registration required. An offer letter carries no SSN, DOB, or account/TIN number; candidate name, employer address, and employer contact are standard sensitivity and promoted for identity/processor reasons, not masking. If a future issuer variant includes the candidate's SSN or home address, that field must be added as a named typed field and registered (raw), never left to the catch-all.
